name: Choy Uyi
tagline: A tea house: loose-leaf tea, teaware and a quiet tea room in the old town

listing.description: A website for a tea shop, tea room or coffee house. A steaming cup on the first screen, teas as labelled tins on a shelf and a brewing ritual with timer rings.

seo.title: Choy Uyi — tea shop and tea room in Tashkent
seo.description: Loose-leaf green, black, oolong and pu-erh, teaware and tastings. A tea room on Sebzor, tea delivery across Uzbekistan, loose tea from 50 g.
seo.answer: Choy Uyi is a tea shop and tea room at 14 Sebzor Street in Tashkent, open daily from 10:00 to 22:00. Loose tea is sold from 50 g: Sencha green tea is 65,000 UZS and Tie Guan Yin oolong 95,000 UZS per 50 g. A pot of tea in the tea room starts at 45,000 UZS, a five-tea tasting is 180,000 UZS, and delivery in Tashkent takes one day.

sections.title: Time to brew
sections.subtitle: Loose-leaf tea from China, Japan, India and Sri Lanka, handmade teaware and a tea room where you can try everything before you buy.

sections.label: The house
sections.title: Tea, unhurried
sections.text: We opened the tea house in an old building on Sebzor so that tea could be a pause again, not a teabag on the run. The shelves hold about 60 teas that we bring directly from small growers and taste ourselves. In the tea room we brew in gaiwans and piyalas, and in the shop we’ll help you choose a tea for your taste and the water you have at home.

items.name: Sencha
items.text: Japan. Grassy, with a sea-breeze freshness.

items.name: Longjing
items.text: China. Roasted chestnut and sweetness.

items.name: Silver Needle
items.text: China. White tea from buds, honey and apricot.

items.name: Tie Guan Yin
items.text: Lilac and cream, steeps up to seven times.

items.name: Da Hong Pao
items.text: A roasted rock oolong, warm and deep.

items.name: Darjeeling
items.text: India, first flush. Muscatel and flowers.

items.name: Shou pu-erh 2016
items.text: Earthy and sweet, warming in winter.

items.name: Sheng pu-erh 2019
items.text: Bright, with a light bitterness and fruit.

items.name: Mountain herbs
items.text: Thyme, mint and rosehip from Chimgan.

items.title: Warm
items.text: Rinse the gaiwan and cups with boiling water: tea opens up in warm ware.

items.title: Wake
items.text: Pour 95° water over 7 g of tea and discard it at once to wake the leaf.

items.title: Steep
items.text: First infusions are 15 seconds each, then 5 seconds longer every time.

items.title: Share
items.text: Pour through a pitcher so everyone’s cup tastes the same.

items.title: A pot of tea
items.text: Any tea from the shelf in a gaiwan or teapot, with refills of water as long as you like.

items.title: Tasting
items.text: Five teas from green to pu-erh, with a tea master guiding you.

items.title: Tea ceremony
items.text: Gongfu cha for up to six people, around an hour and a half.

items.title: Gift set
items.text: Three teas in tins, two cups and a card, wrapped in kraft paper.

items.quote: I came for a gift and left two hours later with three tins and a new favourite oolong. Such a calm place.
items.author: Kamila T.

items.quote: The tasting showed me pu-erh isn’t just ‘earth’. The tea master explains without any snobbery.
items.author: Sanjar Yu.

items.quote: I order tea to Samarkand. It arrives in two days, always with a note on how to brew it.
items.author: Lola N.

items.q: Can I taste a tea before buying it?
items.a: Yes. We’ll brew any tea from the shelf for you to try; it’s free with a purchase of 50 g or more.
In Tashkent the next day for 20,000 UZS, free from 300,000 UZS. Across Uzbekistan by post in 2–4 days.

items.q: Do I need to book a table?
items.a: Usually not on weekdays. For Friday evenings and weekends it’s best to message ahead: we have 12 seats.

items.q: Which tea should a beginner try?
items.a: Start with Tie Guan Yin or Darjeeling: both are easy to like and forgive brewing mistakes.

items.q: How should I store loose tea?
items.a: In a closed tin, in the dark and away from spices. Drink green tea within six months; pu-erh can keep for years.
